findings.title: Session verification window renders a false 'Your session has ended' (client-side session claim)
findings.claim: Both pages show the unauthorized state whenever memberToken is null, without checking memberChecking. Core sets memberToken to null while it verifies a session, so a signed-in customer is told their session ended. This client-side session claim is new in this change; before, only the server's result could produce 'unauthorized'.
findings.evidence: OrderHistory.tsx:59-60@e3b551f and OrderHistoryDetail.tsx:55-56@e3b551f: `!memberToken ? { phase: "unauthorized" }`. core.tsx:186-187@e3b551f starts with token null and status 'checking'. core.tsx:298,308 null the token and set 'checking' on every verification, which runs on SIGNED_IN/TOKEN_REFRESHED/USER_UPDATED (core.tsx:426-435). kit.tsx:687-694 renders 'Please sign in.' / 'Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.' with a Member Login button. Sibling convention shows loading while checking: Dashboard.tsx:241-242, AccountOrderDetail.tsx:23-24@e3b551f. The test mock (test:21) supplies only memberToken, so no test covers this. Failure scenario: a signed-in customer hard-loads /research/member/order-history (or a detail URL) and sees 'session has ended' until /api/research/member/me returns. On each hourly TOKEN_REFRESHED, loaded history switches to the sign-in prompt before reloading.
findings.fix: In both components, destructure memberChecking from useResearch and derive `memberChecking ? loading : !memberToken ? unauthorized : snapshot match ? snapshot.state : loading`. Keep the no-request rule while checking or the token is null (the effect already returns early). Add tests in the new file: (a) memberChecking=true with token null shows ra-loading, does not show 'Please sign in.' and makes no adapter call; (b) loaded A -> checking/null -> A' (refreshed token) never shows the sign-in prompt or A's stale data; (c) checking -> signed_out with token null shows 'Please sign in.'.

verdicts.note: Confirmed. OrderHistory.tsx:59-60@e3b551f and OrderHistoryDetail.tsx:55-56@e3b551f show the unauthorized state whenever memberToken is null, and neither reads memberChecking. Core starts with the token null and the status 'checking' (core.tsx:186-188). establishMemberSession nulls the token and sets 'checking' (core.tsx:296-308) on initial hydration, on every token change, and whenever verification is forced. kit.tsx:687-694 then shows 'Please sign in.' / 'Your session has ended.' with a Member Login button. Sibling pages show loading while checking (Dashboard.tsx:241@e3b551f, AccountOrderDetail.tsx:11,23@e3b551f), so the page contradicts the session authority. Two precision corrections. (1) The checker calls this 'new in this change'. That is true of where the claim comes from, but customers already saw it: the parent ran listCanonicalOrders(null), sent no Authorization header, and the server answered 401 'unauthorized' (server/research/orders/http.ts:76-77@e3b551f). Worse, the parent could end stuck on that prompt when the stale 401 arrived after the token-bearing success. The new code removes that race, so this is a defect left in a derivation the change rewrote, not a new regression. (2) The checker says this happens on 'every SIGNED_IN'. In fact a SIGNED_IN with an unchanged token and a member present returns early without nulling (core.tsx:283). The token is nulled on initial hydration, on a SIGNED_IN with a new token, on TOKEN_REFRESHED (a new JWT) and on USER_UPDATED (forced). The proposed fix is safe: memberSessionStatus always leaves 'checking' (core.tsx:271,328,345,350,366,373,378,483,493), so 'loading while checking' cannot spin forever. P2 stands. The package's purpose is truthful session-continuity states, the false prompt is visible on hard load and on every hourly refresh, and the fix takes one line per component.

The copy concern holds. The server emits a coded 404 order_not_found (server/research/orders/http.ts:108,113@e3b551f). adapter.ts:24 calls apiGet without knownNotFoundDenials, so api.ts:110-124 discards that code and returns unavailable. OrderHistoryDetail.tsx:129-130,252-260 then promises a transient fault ('right now', 'try again later') with a retry that cannot succeed for a missing order, or for an uncoded 403. The 'records misstate the limit' part is weaker than the checker says: handoff:115@6a995c5 does name the cause ('Canonical adapter does not opt into knownNotFoundDenials'), and the component genuinely never receives a missing-record signal. The real imprecisions are calling the server's coded 404 'generic' and not saying that the server emits order_not_found at all. Latent either way: createCanonicalOrderRouteTable has no mount outside its definition at e3b551f, so clients currently get SPA HTML 200, which maps to unavailable.

Confirmed pre-existing and unchanged: the diff does not touch OrderHistory.tsx:83-85,190-191. A server 503 order_history_unavailable (a failed durable read, http.ts:86-90) maps to unavailable because api.ts checks the status first (api.ts:110-125), and the page then shows 'not available yet... switched on... no order has been lost' with no retry control (kit.tsx:686). Addition: the new test at test:397-406 asserts 'Order history is not available yet.', which locks this copy in, and that test passes against the parent. Keep it as a named limit of this package.

Each sub-claim checks out. (a) test:269-279 only catches removal of the try/catch: without the active guard, a publish on an unmounted instance does nothing. (b) Correct, but incomplete: the reject variant of test:211-229 also passes against the parent and fails only through Vitest's unhandled-error policy, since loading, no STALE-A and dataAccess-not-called all still hold. vitest.config.ts@e3b551f has no override for that policy. (c) Correct: no control separates useLayoutEffect from useEffect, because the display guarantee is the render-time identity match. (d) Correct: denied renders inside the boundary's ok branch, and the list's unavailable state renders ResearchEmptyState with no action, so harness.retry drives transitions no user can trigger. Further notes: test:128-135 and test:397-406 are preservation controls that also pass against the parent, so they should not be counted as regression discriminators. If the real-adapter control at test:382-394 does not settle within act(), it fails rather than falsely passing.

Confirmed and fail-safe. If React discarded the useMemo cache, the request object would differ, render would show loading, and the effect would run again. No other identity's data could appear. Record it as a named limit, or move the identity into state or a ref.

verify.opinion:
OH-1 stands as a P2 correction. While core is verifying a session, it sets memberToken to null and reports 'checking'. Both pages treat that null token as a signed-out session and tell a signed-in customer 'Your session has ended.' This happens on hard load, on a sign-in with a new token, on the hourly token refresh and on USER_UPDATED. Sibling pages already show loading in this state. The fix is one line per component plus three tests, and it is safe because the session status always leaves 'checking'.

Everything else in the isolation design is sound. Render-time identity matching plus a per-lifetime active flag means no other identity's or order's data can be shown. Stale results cannot overwrite current ones. No request is sent without a token. Adapter, server and status/economics bytes are unchanged, and scope and bindings match the registration exactly.

Two precision points on OH-1. The customer-visible false prompt already existed in the parent, through a request sent with no token that the server answered with 401, and the new code removes the parent's stale-401 race. The checker's 'every SIGNED_IN' overstates it, because core.tsx:283 skips the reset when the token is unchanged.

OH-2 through OH-5 stand as P3. OH-2's 'records misstate' part is softened because the handoff names the adapter opt-in gap. I found two further P3 test-labelling items.

Disposition: CORRECTIONS_REQUIRED for OH-1. Once OH-1 is fixed with its tests, I would accept the package with named limits: OH-2/OH-3 wording, the useMemo fail-safe, tests authored but not run, and pages that are not yet mounted.

check.summary:
I reviewed the source only. Nothing was executed, and the authored tests are NOT RUN. Source commit 6bd576c (parent 71e4cc4) changes exactly the two registered paths. Its tree is 16e9afb and its blobs are 26e9d94 (11891 bytes) and 63896a0 (17241 bytes). Those committed bytes contain no CR characters, and the blobs and sizes match the registration. Records commit a5271e6 sits directly on 6bd576c and changes only five .xenios paths; the two source blobs are identical there. I found no P0, P1 or P2 defect.

How the fix works: Apply now keys a per-principal ApplicationForm on [memberToken, Boolean(member), member.cartScope] (Apply.tsx:42-43@6bd576c), so a token switch, scope switch, sign-out or member removal replaces all form and outcome state in the same commit. Each instance POSTs only with its own token prop (Apply.tsx:50,109), so a stale result can only land on an unmounted instance, and React discards that update.

What is preserved and what improved:
- The receipt shows the immutable submitted snapshot (Apply.tsx:98-104,111,134), not later edits.
- The fixed research_rep role (Apply.tsx:99), the pending agreement (accepted={false}, Apply.tsx:212) and the canonical adapter, endpoint and Bearer authorization are unchanged.
- The old copy implying email delivery ("A confirmation will be sent to ...") was removed.
- An unexpected adapter throw now yields a truthful unconfirmed message, and there is no automatic replay.
- All test traffic goes through stubbed fetch or a spied adapter, so there is no live POST or email.

The authored tests do catch the key regressions: removing the identity key, rendering the receipt from the mutable email field, the old state-based duplicate guard, and the missing catch. They overstate coverage in two places: the attempt-ownership guards (PA-1) and the trim claim (PA-3). There is also one plausible liveness edge case in the layout cleanup (PA-2) and one labelling issue in the records (PA-4). All four are P3.

Named limits:
- A routine Supabase token refresh remounts the form for the same principal. This discards drafts, a displayed receipt, or an in-flight outcome, with no unconfirmed notice. The handoff discloses this.
- A realistic connection loss still shows the adapter's "The connection failed. Please try again."
- The adapter's default "The team will follow up by email." can still appear on the receipt.

findings.title: The source-test map credits the tests with proving the attempt-ownership guards, but no test fails if those guards are removed
findings.claim: The sourceTestMap entry 'Suppress obsolete asynchronous outcomes' says tests 254-272, 316-347 and 362-379 prove the per-instance attempt identity, the layout cleanup and the ownership checks in success, catch and finally (Apply.tsx:61,110,113,119@6bd576c). None of those tests would fail if the guards were deleted. Only the synchronous in-flight check at Apply.tsx:74 is discriminated.
findings.evidence: In every cross-identity case the keyed remount (Apply.tsx:42-43@6bd576c) means the old closure updates an unmounted instance, and React discards that update whatever the ref holds. apply.test.tsx:362-379@6bd576c goes further: it unmounts the whole root (:367) and renders the replacement in a new createRoot (via renderApply, :98-103), so it isolates trivially and would also pass against parent 71e4cc4. Within one mounted instance a second attempt cannot start while the first is pending (Apply.tsx:74), so the checks at 110 and 113 are unreachable except in the PA-2 case. Test :349-360 does discriminate line 74.
findings.fix: Restate the map: attribute stale-outcome suppression to the keyed remount, and describe lines 61, 110, 113 and 119 as defensive and untested. Alternatively remove them (see PA-2). If they stay, add a test that tears down layout effects without unmounting the instance.

findings.title: The layout cleanup clears the active attempt on any layout-effect teardown, which can leave a mounted form stuck on 'Submitting...'
findings.claim: Apply.tsx:61@6bd576c clears activeAttempt whenever layout effects are torn down, not only on unmount, and the setup function restores nothing. If that teardown happens while the same-principal instance stays mounted with a POST pending, lines 110 and 113 drop the result. The outcome then stays 'submitting', the button stays disabled (Apply.tsx:253), and no unconfirmed notice appears. This is not a false success. The verdict is PLAUSIBLE: I have not proven the trigger is reachable in this app.
findings.evidence: React 18+ destroys layout effects when an already-revealed Suspense boundary re-suspends outside a transition, and re-runs setup on reveal; React's Activity component does the same. Apply sits inside a Suspense boundary (section.tsx:211-215,407@6bd576c, the L wrapper). The key at Apply.tsx:42-43 already isolates identities, so this cleanup adds no identity protection; its only effect beyond unmount is this case.
findings.fix: Remove the cleanup and rely on the keyed instance. Or track mount state in the setup function and, if a pending attempt was orphaned, set the existing unconfirmed error instead of leaving 'submitting'.

findings.title: The 'original trimmed receipt email' claim is met by the email input's own sanitization, so the component's .trim() is untested
findings.claim: Test apply.test.tsx:229-252@6bd576c enters '  original@example.com  ' and expects 'original@example.com' in the body and the receipt. The type=email input strips leading and trailing whitespace before React's onChange reads the value, so the .trim() at Apply.tsx:101@6bd576c is not exercised. The snapshot-versus-edit property itself is discriminated.
findings.evidence: The input is type="email" (Apply.tsx:167@6bd576c). The test sets the value through the prototype setter (apply.test.tsx:121-129). The HTML value-sanitization algorithm for type=email strips newlines and leading and trailing ASCII whitespace; I believe jsdom implements it, but that is unconfirmed here because tests are NOT RUN, so this is PLAUSIBLE.
findings.fix: Drop 'trimmed' from the map's test claim, or check the trim against a field that is not sanitized. The behaviour is harmless as written.

findings.title: The handoff pairs git blob ids with working-tree byte counts and hashes without labelling which is which
findings.claim: In records a5271e6, the handoff sourceFiles list each git blob id next to bytes and a rawSha256 that come from the CRLF working-tree copy, not the committed bytes, and gives no digest domain. The registration copy labels these correctly.
findings.evidence: In the handoff at a5271e6, sourceFiles shows Apply.tsx with bytes 12155 and rawSha256 ad739f..., and apply.test.tsx with 17643 and 31b80c..., each beside its gitBlob id. The committed blobs are 11891 and 17241 bytes with 0 CR characters (cat-file -s and wc -c at 6bd576c). 12155 is 11891 plus 264 lines and 17643 is 17241 plus 402 lines, which is consistent with CRLF materialization. The registration labels these values receivedWorkingTreeBinding, with differentNewlineMaterializationDisclosed set to true.
findings.fix: In a later records revision, label the digest domain in the handoff sourceFiles, or cite the committed raw bytes alongside the blob ids.

deviations: Named limit, disclosed in the handoff: a TOKEN_REFRESHED event (core.tsx:426-435@6bd576c) calls establishMemberSession, which briefly sets member and memberToken to null (core.tsx:296-299@6bd576c). That changes the form key, so a same-principal routine refresh discards drafts, a displayed receipt, or an in-flight outcome. The in-flight case shows no unconfirmed notice. The Apply route is not member-gated (section.tsx:407@6bd576c uses L with member=false), so in the parent this page did not remount on refresh. Server-side duplicate rejection on an explicit resubmit is NOT PROVEN.

Named limit, adapter-owned and out of scope: a real connection loss on the current attempt never reaches the component catch. apiPost catches the fetch failure (lib/api.ts:146-147@6bd576c) and returns the error 'The connection failed. Please try again.' through submitPartnerRequest. The new unconfirmed copy therefore covers only unexpected adapter throws, and the deferredFetch 'connection rejection' case (apply.test.tsx:182@6bd576c) exercises the adapter mapping, not Apply.tsx:112-117.

Named limit, adapter-owned: when the server returns no message (as in every test fixture), the receipt renders the adapter's default 'Received. The team will follow up by email.' (partner.ts:277@6bd576c). It is a follow-up commitment, not a delivery claim, and no test asserts against it.

The spy-based tests (apply.test.tsx:362-401@6bd576c) do not stub fetch as a guard. Any unexpected extra call would reach the real adapter with a relative URL and be caught, so there is no live POST, but there is also no explicit guard.
The raw SHA-256 of the committed bytes was not recomputed under the allowed tooling: NOT PROVEN. Blob ids, sizes and the LF-only content are verified.
Server-side authorization, one-partner-per-member enforcement, idempotency and email behaviour were not examined: NOT PROVEN.
All authored tests are NOT RUN. Whether they discriminate was judged statically.

verdicts.note: Upheld, with one correction. The keyed remount at Apply.tsx:42-43@6bd576c alone produces every cross-identity test result. Updates from an old closure go to a deleted fiber, which React drops. Deleting the layout cleanup (Apply.tsx:61) or the ownership conditions (110, 113, the `=== attempt` test at 119) would not fail any test. apply.test.tsx:362-379 also uses a fresh createRoot, and its resolve case would pass against the parent. The correction: the checker lists 119 as undiscriminated, but the clearing itself is discriminated. Without it, the explicit retry in apply.test.tsx:381-401@6bd576c is blocked by the guard at line 74 and calledTimes(2) fails. Only the condition on line 119 is untested, and test :349-360 discriminates the line-74 ref check. The comment at Apply.tsx:59-60 is also misleading: a replacement instance has its own ref and can never observe the old one.

Upheld as PLAUSIBLE, with a concrete path the checker did not name. (1) Every partner route renders <L> at the same Switch position (section.tsx:341,407-422@6bd576c). The Switch returns a keyless cloned Route, so the L fiber and its Suspense boundary (section.tsx:211-217) are reused when moving between partner pages. (2) The form's Back link (Apply.tsx:256, PARTNER_ROUTES.home = /research/partners, routes.ts:118) stays enabled while the request is submitting. (3) section.tsx has no startTransition, so this navigation is a synchronous update. If the PartnerLanding chunk is not yet loaded, the already-shown boundary suspends again, hides Apply and runs the cleanup at Apply.tsx:61. (4) If the user returns to /apply before the chunk loads, the same fiber reappears still marked 'submitting' with a null ref. Lines 110 and 113 then drop the result and the button stays disabled (Apply.tsx:253). The parent would have applied the result to the hidden fiber. This is not a false success. I have not shown the path is reachable at runtime, so it stays P3.

Upheld as PLAUSIBLE. The email input is type="email" (Apply.tsx:167@6bd576c), and setById uses the prototype value setter (apply.test.tsx:121-129). Value sanitization therefore strips the surrounding spaces before React reads onChange, so the .trim() at Apply.tsx:101 is never exercised. The legalName and audience trims are not exercised either, because the fixtures have no surrounding whitespace. The snapshot-versus-edit property remains discriminated.

Upheld and verified. The handoff's sourceFiles at a5271e6 pair blobs 26e9d94 and 63896a0 with bytes 12155 and 17643 and with working-tree rawSha256 values, and give no digest-domain label. cat-file -s gives 11891 and 17241, and the Apply.tsx blob contains 0 CR characters. Line counts are 264 and 402, so 11891+264=12155 and 17241+402=17643, which is consistent with CRLF materialization. The registration copy labels both domains correctly (RAW_COMMITTED_GIT_BYTES versus receivedWorkingTreeBinding RAW_PHYSICAL_WORKING_TREE_BYTES). This is a records-precision issue only.

verify.opinion:
I reviewed the source only; nothing was executed, and the authored tests are NOT RUN. I agree with the checker's disposition, ACCEPTED_WITH_NAMED_LIMITS, and found no P0, P1 or P2 defect. Scope and bindings check out independently. Source 6bd576c changes exactly Apply.tsx and apply.test.tsx. The tree is 16e9afb and the blobs are 26e9d94 (11891 bytes, LF-only) and 63896a0 (17241 bytes). Records a5271e6 sits directly on the source with tree 778da24 and touches only five .xenios paths. The adapter, core and lib files are unchanged.

What the fix guarantees, and why:
- Isolation comes entirely from keying ApplicationForm on [memberToken, Boolean(member), cartScope] (Apply.tsx:42-43@6bd576c).
- Any change of identity deletes the old fiber in the same commit, and React drops late updates sent to a deleted fiber.
- This identity is stricter than the principal: each bearer token counts as its own identity. That is the safe direction for isolation, and it is consistent with core.tsx publishing no principal data while a new token is verified.
- The receipt is rendered from the immutable submitted snapshot.
- An unexpected throw yields truthful unconfirmed copy, and nothing replays automatically.
- The research_rep role, the pending agreement, the canonical endpoint and the Bearer authorization are unchanged.
- The old copy implying email delivery is removed.

All four checker findings are upheld at P3:
- PA-1 needs one correction: the clearing in finally is discriminated by :381-401; only its ownership condition is not.
- PA-2 is strengthened with a concrete path. The partner routes share one reused L/Suspense boundary, and the Back link stays enabled while submitting. Navigating to an unloaded chunk then coming back can leave the form stuck on 'Submitting...'. That is a liveness regression against the parent, not a false success.
- PA-3 is plausible: the email input's own sanitization trims the value, so the component's trim is not exercised.
- PA-4 is verified by the arithmetic: 11891+264=12155 and 17241+402=17643.

I add two P3 items:
- PAV-1: the pending agreement and the non-approval copy are not test-pinned, though the map implies they are.
- PAV-2: the same-principal reset also fires on USER_UPDATED and refreshMember, not only on token refresh, and the 'token switch' test pins it as required behavior.

The remaining limits are the adapter-owned ones the checker named, plus the adapter mapping of a 2xx JSON body without both ok:false and a code to 'accepted'.
deviations: Tests are NOT RUN. Whether they discriminate was judged statically, and no pass counts are claimed or inferred.
The raw SHA-256 of the committed bytes was not recomputed under the allowed tooling: NOT PROVEN. Blob ids, sizes, the CR count (0 for Apply.tsx), line counts and trees were verified with git.

PA-2 rests on React 19 Suspense semantics (React ^19.2.0 and wouter ^3.3.5 per package.json@6bd576c): hiding a re-suspended boundary runs layout cleanup, and Switch returns a keyless cloned Route. Whether it is reachable at runtime is NOT PROVEN.
PA-3 assumes jsdom ^29.1.1 implements type=email value sanitization: NOT PROVEN without execution.

Whether vi.spyOn on the ESM namespace intercepts calls under Vitest ^4.1.10 is NOT PROVEN. The precedent is Campaigns.test.tsx:124,165@6bd576c. A failed intercept would make :381 fail loudly and :362 pass silently, with no live POST in either case.

Out of scope and pre-existing: api.ts:139-145@6bd576c maps a 2xx JSON body without both ok:false and a string code to 'ok', and partner.ts:276-278 then shows 'Application received.' What the server actually returns is NOT PROVEN.
Server-side authorization, one-partner-per-member enforcement, duplicate handling on an explicit resubmit, idempotency and email behaviour were not examined: NOT PROVEN.
Not a finding: the bearer token appears in the React key. It is already present as a prop and in the context value, so the key adds no new exposure.

I considered and rejected initial-hydration draft loss: the section holds the gate in 'checking' until refreshMember finishes (core.tsx:496-500@6bd576c), so the form is not interactive during the first verification.

Only git show, diff, rev-parse and cat-file (piped to grep, sed, head or wc) and Read on the registration copy were used. No files were created, modified or deleted, and no interpreter, test, build, MCP tool or network call was used.
